newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - May 6.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on May 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The consortium set up to the exploit the controversial Busang gold find in East Kalimantan has been disbanded after it was found that the property contained small and uneconomic amounts of gold.

Ismail Hasan Matereum, head of the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP), said that up to now he has no plans to meet Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
The government and the three authorised political parties agreed there had been an abundance of rule infringements in the first nine days of the 27-day general election campaign.

Prosecutors have sought a five-year jail term for television actress Zarina who is being prosecuted for the possession of the drug Ecstasy. Zarina was deported from the United States after she escaped from police custody in Jakarta.
Streets in the capital Jakarta were blocked as thousands of PPP supporters paraded in motorcades of trucks, buses, cars and motorcycles in violation of election campaign regulations.

The Coordinating Minister for Economics and Finance Saleh Afif said that 13 local banks would participate in the $1.3 billion loan to aspiring carmaker PT Timor Putra Nasional, a joint venture between the Humpuss group and KIA Motors of South Korea.
